obligations.title: Usability Engineering Plan
obligations.verbatim: Establish and maintain a usability engineering process. The process must be integrated with the overall design and development process. Usability engineering activities must be traceable to the risk management process (ISO 14971).
extracted_requirements: Establish a usability engineering process and maintain it throughout the development lifecycle
Integrate the usability engineering process with the design and development process (DDP)
Ensure traceability between usability engineering activities and the risk management process

obligations.title: Use Specification
obligations.verbatim: Identify and characterize intended users. Consider: clinical role, training level, experience, physical capabilities.
extracted_requirements: Identify and characterize the intended users for each use scenario
Consider user attributes including clinical role, training level, prior experience with similar devices, and physical capabilities
Document separate user profiles per module where user populations differ

obligations.title: User Profiles & Environments
obligations.verbatim: Document the use environment for each use scenario. Consider: lighting, noise, sterility, time pressure, distractions, PPE.
extracted_requirements: Document the intended use environment for each module

extracted_requirements.Address: ambient lighting, noise level, sterility requirements, time pressure, concurrent distractions, required PPE

extracted_requirements: Distinguish between OR and non-OR environments — Intra-Op operates in a sterile surgical field, Pre-Op in a clinic office

obligations.title: Use-Related Risk Analysis
obligations.verbatim: Identify hazards and hazardous situations related to use. Identify potential use errors and their causes. Evaluate the severity and probability of harm from use errors. Feed use-related risks into the ISO 14971 risk management process.
extracted_requirements: Identify all potential use errors per module — perception errors, cognitive errors, action errors
Identify the hazardous situation and potential harm sequence for each use error
Evaluate severity and probability of harm from each use error
Feed use-related risks into the ISO 14971 risk management process (risk inputs, not standalone)

extracted_requirements.Critical use error categories for SaMD: misread measurements, missed alerts, incorrect plan selection, wrong patient data confirmation

obligations.title: User Interface Specification
obligations.verbatim: Establish the user interface specification from use specification and risk analysis. Specify: information presentation, controls, navigation, feedback, error prevention. Include measurable acceptance criteria for critical use scenarios.
extracted_requirements: Establish a UI specification derived from the use specification and use-related risk analysis

extracted_requirements.Specify: information presentation, controls, navigation, feedback mechanisms, error prevention features

extracted_requirements: Define measurable acceptance criteria for critical use scenarios (tasks where use error could cause harm)
Critical use scenarios must be explicitly identified and flagged in the specification

obligations.title: UI Verification
obligations.verbatim: Verify the user interface meets the user interface specification. Include inspection, analysis, and testing methods. Verify risk control measures related to usability are implemented.
extracted_requirements: Verify the implemented user interface meets the UI specification requirements
Use inspection, analysis, and testing methods as appropriate
Verify that all usability-related risk control measures from the use-related risk analysis are implemented and effective

obligations.title: Formative Usability Evaluation
obligations.verbatim: Evaluate the user interface with representative users in representative environments (formative phase). Methods: cognitive walkthrough, heuristic evaluation, usability testing with think-aloud. Can be done with simulated environments and prototype interfaces. Multiple rounds expected.
extracted_requirements: Conduct iterative formative usability evaluations during design
Use representative users (or similar proxies) in representative or simulated environments

extracted_requirements.Methods include: cognitive walkthrough, heuristic evaluation, think-aloud usability testing

extracted_requirements: Multiple rounds expected — findings must be fed back into design changes
Document findings, design changes made in response, and rationale for accepted vs. deferred findings

obligations.title: Summative Usability Validation
obligations.verbatim: Evaluate the user interface with representative users in representative environments (summative phase). Must use production-equivalent device in representative use environment. Must include statistical evidence that critical tasks can be completed safely. Deliverable: Summative Usability Evaluation Report.
extracted_requirements: Conduct a final summative usability evaluation before market release
Use production-equivalent device and representative use environment (or validated simulation)
Include representative users — matching the intended user profiles defined in §5.1.1
Evaluate all critical tasks defined in the UI specification
Demonstrate with statistical evidence (task completion rates, error rates) that critical tasks can be completed safely

extracted_requirements.Document: participant profiles, tasks tested, acceptance criteria, results, use errors observed and their root cause

extracted_requirements: Summative Usability Evaluation Report is required in the 510(k) submission for Class II SaMD

obligations.title: UOUP Evaluation
obligations.verbatim: If reusing an existing user interface or UI components, evaluate them using this process. Applicable when using third-party UI frameworks or pre-built components in the clinical interface.
extracted_requirements: If third-party UI frameworks or pre-built components are used in the clinical interface, evaluate them under the UOUP process
UOUP evaluation requires demonstrating that reused UI components meet the usability requirements for the device's intended use
Document the evaluation rationale — what was evaluated, how, and what was accepted or rejected
